# B2. Other countries {#oecd-countries}

## What shapes pensions, savings and labor supply in the U.S. and the UK {#oecd-hosts}

The figure repeats the paper's figure {{< var p.fig_US_overview >}} with the UK beside the U.S. Each host keeps its
own calibration and changes one characteristic over the whole horizon. The characteristics are its design, moved to
the two corners; its population growth, halved (mild ageing) or held at one (acute ageing); or France's income
distribution, voting patterns or taste for leisure, with France's households cut at the host's income percentiles.
On both hosts ageing and the design move the tax rate most. Ageing and France's voting patterns move the UK's tax
rate by less than the U.S. one at every IES, and so does the design up to an IES of one. Two rows change sign
between the hosts. France's income distribution raises the UK's tax rate where it lowers the U.S. one, because at
the UK's income cuts France is the more unequal of the two (appendix {{< var p.app_US >}}). France's taste for
leisure lengthens the UK's workweek where it shortens the U.S. one, since France's average taste for leisure lies
between the two hosts'.

::: {.oa-explorer .column-page}
{{< include _generated/exhibits/OECD_Hosts-head.qmd >}}

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
import {counterfactuals, control, ROWS_GIVEN, RHO, GIVEN_OUTCOMES} from "./assets/oa.js"
oecd = FileAttachment("_generated/data/OECD_Counterfactuals.csv").csv({typed: true})
oecdMain = oecd.filter(d => d.source === "main" && d.calibration === "commonX" && d.effect === "full")
viewof b2Out = control("radio", GIVEN_OUTCOMES, {key: "hosts", label: "Outcome", value: "tau"})
counterfactuals(oecdMain, {rows: ROWS_GIVEN, series: RHO, outcome: b2Out, width,
  facets: [{label: "U.S.", filter: d => d.host === "US"}, {label: "UK", filter: d => d.host === "UK"}]})
```

{{< include _generated/exhibits/OECD_Hosts-foot.qmd >}}
:::

## The UK at U.S. income groups {#oecd-regroup}

The paper cuts the UK's households at the UK's own income groups, which identify θ from the replacement rates at
half-mean and mean income. It cuts France at the U.S. percentiles, so that its households replace the U.S. ones type
by type, and regroups France at the UK's cuts for the UK as host. The table sets the groupings side by side.
Regrouping changes what the calibration reads: θ is read off the replacement rates at other cuts, ω follows, and the
productivity spread is that of other groups. At the U.S. cuts the UK's productivity spread is much narrower than at
its own, while France's at the UK's cuts is wider than at the U.S. ones. The UK at the U.S. cuts is a linear fit of
the UK's group means against cumulative population shares rather than a recount of the survey, so its spread is an
approximation. The tabs give the two regroupings household by household.

{{< include _generated/exhibits/OECD_Regroupings.qmd >}}

::: {.panel-tabset}
### The UK at U.S. income groups
{{< include _generated/exhibits/UKUS_householdheterogeneity.qmd >}}

### France at the UK's income groups
{{< include _generated/exhibits/FRUK_householdheterogeneity.qmd >}}
:::

The figure imposes the counterfactuals of the first figure on the UK under the two groupings, France's households
cut at the same groups as the host's. Ageing moves the two alike, since it does not depend on how households are
grouped. The design and France's voting patterns move the regrouped UK much less: at the U.S. cuts its incomes are
compressed, so a flat benefit redistributes little and the poor have little to gain from voting more. France's income
distribution, conversely, raises the regrouped UK's tax rate by much more, because next to that compressed
distribution France's is unequal.

::: {.oa-explorer .column-page}
{{< include _generated/exhibits/OECD_Groupings-head.qmd >}}

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof b2gOut = control("radio", GIVEN_OUTCOMES, {key: "groups", label: "Outcome", value: "tau"})
counterfactuals(oecdMain, {rows: ROWS_GIVEN, series: RHO, outcome: b2gOut, width,
  facets: [{label: "UK, its own income groups", filter: d => d.host === "UK"},
           {label: "UK, U.S. income groups", filter: d => d.host === "UKUS"}]})
```
